newsitem.title: UK: Fewer UK households see better economy in '97 - GfK.
newsitem.headline: Fewer UK households see better economy in '97 - GfK.

text.p: Only 21 percent of British households expect the UK's economic situation to improve over the next 12 months, November's European Commission confidence survey shows.
The survey, conducted by GfK, showed 20 percent of households surveyed expected the economic environment to improve a little while only one percent forecast a large improvement.
October's survey showed 22 percent expected some improvement with two percent expecting it to be significant.
The largest number of households, 45 percent, expect the economic situation to stay roughly the same, up from 38 percent in October. Only 17 percent expected conditions to deteriorate.

Looking at the UK economy over the past 12 months, 41 percent of the households surveyed said conditions had stayed fairly constant, 22 percent said they had seen a little improvement and two percent said the economy had got much better.
About three in 10 households said things had got worse to some degree.

Turning to individual finances, 19 percent of households said they expect their finances to improve to some extent in the next year but 60 percent anticipated little change. 21 percent said they had picked up over the past 12 months.
